component_decisions.scope: Genuine finite multivariate Gaussian probability and full support from positive covariance
component_decisions.mathematical_reason: The standard Euclidean Gaussian is genuinely the toLp pushforward of independent unit-variance Gaussian coordinates. The previously proved real Gaussian full-support body and finite product full-support instance apply to that probability measure. WithLp toLp is surjective and continuous in the product-induced topology. Positive covariance supplies an actual invertible CFC square root, by its nonnegative-unit equivalence and the positive matrix unit theorem. The actual Euclidean matrix action is continuous and surjective, so translation plus this action maps full support onto full support. The probability assertion also holds for other covariance inputs because the actual definition is a measurable Gaussian pushforward; full support and covariance identities require the explicit positive factors.

component_decisions.scope: Provided matrix-normal law has actual V tensor U covariance and true(A,B) coordinates
component_decisions.mathematical_reason: PosteriorIndex is exactly Fin5 columns times Fin4 rows. The actual latent multivariateGaussian(mean,V tensor U) is defined explicitly. The mapping sends its first four columns to A and last column to B; inverse coordinates are constructed with actual Fin.snoc, not supplied as a desired bijection. The complete fin-snoc proofs establish each coordinate equality. Continuity is proved for the original finite product Plant topology; CStar matrix norm notation is confined to the Gaussian square-root section. The genuine covariance-evaluation proof uses the CFC square-root square identity, Gaussian integrability, and Euclidean basis covariance. The genuine covariance-map proof applies actual measurable maps and coordinate functions, deriving V[j,jprime]*U[i,iprime] for the recovered (A,B). Positive U,V make the Kronecker positive definite by real nonnegative Gram factors and the explicit invertible Kronecker matrix. This establishes a provided matrix-normal law; it does not identify that law with a GP derivative conditional posterior.
